summary: Across DepMap/Sanger mass-spectrometry and CCLE protein-abundance datasets, AAMP abundance correlates with HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1. These correlations do not establish direct binding or HSP90-dependent client behavior.

This source maps ZNHIT2, AAR2, PRPF8, and RUVBL1-RUVBL2 complexes in the PRPF8/U5 snRNP biogenesis pathway and places them in the R2TP-HSP90 chaperone context. It supports R2TP/PRPF8 complex-context evidence, but the primary inspected experiments do not directly test HSP90 isoforms or HSP90 binding to each queued gene.
AARS is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.
Supplementary Figure S13B reports no significant HSP90alpha lactylation after heat stress, whereas the AARS1-regulated K275 mechanism is demonstrated for HSP90beta.
The protein is recovered in PU-H71 HSP90 affinity-proteomics networks in cancer cells.
The cited source resolves HSP90AA1 in the ACE2-centered Affinity Capture-MS result.
HSP90AA1 is identified with ACSL4/DRP1 ferroptosis machinery, including an alpha-specific peptide and co-immunoprecipitation support.
ACTG1 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.
ACTN1 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.

Table S1 identifies HSP90AA1 clone CCSB_8199 among the non-autoactivating DNA-binding baits. Table S2 records HSP90AA1 and ADAMTSL4 in the final NN1.0 network after pooled screening and pairwise backmating. The NN1.0ext occurrence is inherited from NN1.0, and ADAMTSL4 was not included in the mammalian DULIP validation subset. This is one exact binary Y2H association, not multiple studies.
Cytosolic Hsp90 associates with alpha2C-adrenergic receptor and restrains receptor trafficking to the cell surface.

Pan-Hsp90 co-immunoprecipitates with endogenous GRK2, and geldanamycin disrupts the complex, lowers GRK2 abundance, accelerates loss of newly synthesized GRK2, and increases insoluble and proteasome-sensitive GRK2. Purified Hsp90 does not alter mature GRK2 kinase activity, supporting a folding/maturation interpretation rather than acute catalytic regulation.

Supplementary Table 1 resolves exact HSP90AA1 in the AR (Rpn13/ADRM1-Rpn11) cross-link-assisted dual-bait proteasome sample: P07900 is recovered in one technical run from each of two biological replicates.

Affinity-purification mass spectrometry for SPATA5 (AFG2A) reports HSP90AA1: SPATA5 replicate 1: 3 unique/3 total peptides and intensity 610,000 versus no EV detection; replicate 2: 3/3 peptides and intensity 140,000 versus no EV detection. This supports co-recovery with the ATPase complex, not direct contact or client dependence.

Affinity-purification mass spectrometry for SPATA5L1 (AFG2B) reports HSP90AA1: SPATA5L1 replicate 1: 6 unique/7 total peptides and intensity 5,900,000 versus no EV detection; replicate 2: 4/6 peptides and intensity 480,000 versus no EV detection. This supports co-recovery with the ATPase complex, not direct contact or client dependence.
AFP co-immunoprecipitates and colocalizes with a combined HSP90alpha/beta reagent and promotes HSP90-mediated MYC/MET stabilization; the authors classify AFP as an HSP90 cochaperone.

Corrected full text reports plant AGO1-containing RISC assembly depends on HSP90, with CYP40/PP5 and other TPR proteins associating with AGO1 in an HSP90-dependent manner and facilitating RISC maturation.
Single-molecule FRET shows that the Hsp70 and Hsp90 systems cooperatively open and stabilize Drosophila Ago2 for small-RNA loading.

AGO3 has active LUMIER signals to both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms in Taipale 2014, with HSP90AA1 9.796356 and HSP90AB1 9.615581. This supports shared cytosolic HSP90 direct-assay interaction evidence, but it does not show AGO3 folding, stability, maturation, localization, degradation, or activity dependence on HSP90.
Tagged AGO4/EIF2C4 affinity purification identifies the named HSP90 alpha protein by mass spectrometry.

HSP90AA1 is recovered with AGR2 BAP AP-MS in Mia KTEL whole-cell, PANC1 DeltaKTEL whole-cell, and Mia DeltaKTEL spent-media arms. HSP90AA1 is recovered by AGR2 BioID in Mia and MCF7 KTEL and 1-27 whole-cell arms.

Domain-mapping experiments showed that AHR and XAP2 occupy distinct regions of Hsp90: radiolabeled AHR bound a middle-domain GST-Hsp90 fragment, whereas XAP2 bound the Hsp90 C terminus; AHR also bound XAP2 without Hsp90, and the unliganded cytosolic complex dissociated upon AHR-ARNT activation.

Baker-Williams 2019 shows secreted AHA1/eAHA1 competes with TIMP2 on the extracellular HSP90alpha:MMP2 complex and can displace TIMP2 to reactivate MMP2 activity. This is AHSA1/AHA1 extracellular HSP90alpha co-chaperone/regulatory evidence, not AHSA1 client evidence.
AID associates with both cytosolic Hsp90 isoforms, and Hsp90 inhibition accelerates proteasome-linked AID loss and ubiquitination.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-AIMP2 screen record. AIMP2-DX2 IP-MS -> HSP90AA1 in the top-200 interactome, relative DX2/empty-vector value 0.3005; HSP90AB1 and HSP90B1 also occur later in the list. The bait is the DX2 isoform, and no HSP90-pair validation/client mechanism is shown.

AIP has high-confidence structural and biochemical evidence for binding HSP90 TPR-motif peptides and full-length HSP90beta. Crystal structures resolve AIP TPR bound to HSP90beta EDASRMEEVD peptide, ITC compares HSP90beta, HSP90alpha peptide, HSP70, TOMM20, and PDE4A5 peptide binding, and disease mutations separate chaperone motif binding from client-protein interaction effects.

AIPL1 is supported as an HSP90-dependent co-chaperone for rod PDE6. The source shows nucleotide-dependent AIPL1-HSP90 interaction by co-IP/ELISA, variant-dependent loss of HSP90alpha and HSP90beta binding by Y2H and purified-protein ELISA, and HSP90-dependent PDE6alpha stabilization/redistribution/activity consequences.
AKR1B10 immunoprecipitation identifies HSP90alpha by MS, and co-IP plus purified-protein pull-down confirm an exact-alpha physical interaction.
Akt forms intracellular complexes with Hsp90 and Cdc37; Hsp90 inhibitors shorten Akt half-life, promote proteasome-dependent loss, and reduce Akt-dependent signaling.
Akt forms intracellular complexes with Hsp90 and Cdc37; Hsp90 inhibitors shorten Akt half-life, promote proteasome-dependent loss, and reduce Akt-dependent signaling.

Taipale 2014 reports AKT3 LUMIER signals to both HSP90AA1 10.554312 and HSP90AB1 16.174248, with CDC37 30.165769. This is beta-leaning but shared cytosolic HSP90 direct-assay support. The source does not prove AKT3 folding, stability, degradation, localization, or activity dependence on HSP90.

ALDH18A1 is an exact whole_cell_proteome response after HSP90AA1 knockout (source row 805; KO/EV=1.82768446490083; log2 fold change=0.8700170221379614; P=0.00182562598347; q=0.0428118130430532; increased_in_ko). Matched GSE208005 descriptive RNA direction is increased_in_ko.

Folate-column affinity purification of recombinant human ALDH1L1 from A549 lysate recovered Isoform 1 of HSP90-alpha (IPI00784295.2; score 2550.69) in Table 1; Figure 7 used a non-isoform-specific HSP90 antibody for reciprocal co-IP in NIH3T3 cells and therefore does not independently resolve HSP90AA1.
ALDOA is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.

EML4-ALK coimmunoprecipitated with Hsp90alpha in H3122 cells, was depleted within hours and at low-nanomolar IPI-504 concentrations, and its degradation tracked loss of downstream signaling, growth inhibition, apoptosis, and regression of EML4-ALK-driven xenografts; isogenic expression sensitized HEK293FT cells and tumors.

FLAG-AMBRA1 IP-MS in HT29 cells recovered exact P07900/HSP90AA1 with 31 peptides, 19 unique peptides, Mascot score 1147 versus 168 in pLVX control, and a reported 6.83 ratio. HSP90AA1 is not shown in the AMBRA1-USP7 mechanistic figures and was not validated pairwise.

Taipale 2012 classifies AMHR2 as a strong HSP90 kinase-client screen hit with Hsp90 interaction score 7.08, ganetespib dissociation -2.41, protein level after ganetespib 0.35, and Cdc37 luminescence 8.342208. This supports broad HSP90/Cdc37 client-screen evidence for AMHR2, not HSP90AB1 specificity.

This source supports an HSP90AA1/HSP90alpha-resolved AMPD3-HSP90alpha association and AMPD3/HSP90alpha-dependent ferroptosis pathway output, but it does not support ACSL4 as an HSP90 interactor or client. Fig7 provides AMPD3-HSP90alpha predictions/docking plus AMPD3 IP/co-IP. Fig8-Fig9 show HSP90alpha knockdown reduces AMPD3-overexpression-associated mitochondrial damage/DRP1 signaling and lowers ACSL4/lipid ROS readouts. Fig2/Fig6 place ACSL4 among AMPD3-dependent transcript/protein ferroptosis markers in doxorubicin cardiomyopathy.
Taipale 2012 transcription-factor table calls ANAPC2 an Hsp90 hit with Hsp90 interaction 1.35 and Cdc37 interaction 0.26; no client stability mechanism is shown in this row.
ANLN is an early pan-HSP90-inhibitor-responsive complex recruit, not a canonical depletion-defined client.

Local PDF reports ANP32C in Hsp90-containing complexes, PU-H71 immunoprecipitation of oncogenic Hsp90 complexes, rapid cycloheximide degradation, and atypical stabilization/prevention of ANP32C degradation after PU-H71 or 17-AAG compared with AKT.

Local PDF reports ANP32D together with ANP32C as associated with Hsp90-containing oncogenic complexes, but the source text emphasizes ANP32C for detailed instability and inhibitor-response experiments.

HSP90alpha and ANXA2 reciprocally co-immunoprecipitate in porcine aortic endothelial cells and rat aortic endothelium. High glucose/diabetes increases the complex and cell-surface ANXA2; HSP90alpha overexpression raises surface ANXA2, and geldanamycin reverses the localization change without changing total ANXA2 abundance.

Endogenous Hsp90 coimmunoprecipitated with APAF1 from human 293, HeLa, and Jurkat cells after heat shock and from non-heat-treated 293 cells; Hsp90 abundance increased after heat shock, but the antibody and protein band were not alpha/beta resolved.
Human APE2/APEX2 associates with broad Hsp90 and rapidly loses abundance after ganetespib, with orthologous Hsp82/Hsc82 evidence in yeast.
APH1A associates with broad Hsp90 in the gamma-secretase complex, and Hsp90 knockdown reduces complex abundance and amyloidogenic processing.
APLP2 participates in a broad HSP90-containing competitive complex around TGFBR2 and accelerates TGFBR2 ubiquitination and degradation.

Broad cytosolic Hsp90 co-immunoprecipitates with apoB48 and promotes apoB degradation in cell-free systems: geldanamycin disrupts the complex, Hsp90 immunodepletion preserves apoB, yeast Hsp82 mutation suppresses degradation, and overexpressed human Hsp90beta accelerates apoB100 loss in rat hepatoma cells. The only mammalian isoform-specific construct is beta, not the alpha isoform named by the Picard route.
Separately supplied HSP90alpha and HSP90beta stimulate APOBEC3B-mediated mutational activity, but the paper does not demonstrate pairwise APOBEC3B-HSP90 binding.

Main Figure 7 shows separately expressed HSP90alpha and HSP90beta co-translational association with APOBEC3C; alpha/beta stimulation of APOBEC3C activity is stated but delegated to missing Supplemental Figure 1.
HSP90alpha and HSP90beta each associate with APOBEC3G and directly stimulate purified APOBEC3G deaminase activity; endogenous beta co-IP and inhibitor/stability results provide orthogonal support.
HSP90alpha/HSP86 is also identified in APPNeo-immunoprecipitated complexes specific to the Asp664-cleaved APP C terminus from human Alzheimer-disease brain.

AR immunoprecipitation recovered broad Hsp90 in LNCaP prostate-cancer cells, and Hsp27 antisense knockdown reduced the AR-Hsp90 association while accelerating AR loss, shortening AR half-life, and producing proteasome-sensitive AR degradation. These current results support an AR-Hsp90 client complex, but the primary perturbation is Hsp27 depletion rather than direct HSP90 inhibition and the tested Hsp90 isoform is unresolved.

ARAF is classified as a strong kinase client in the Taipale 2012 workbook, with Hsp90 interaction score 6.47, Cdc37 luminescence 8.488687, ganetespib dissociation -2.37, and protein level 0.23 after ganetespib.

FLAG-ARHGAP24 affinity-purification MS identifies HSP90AA1/P07900 as rank 3 with -10lgP 408.91 in Supplementary Table S1; HSP90AB1 is separately rank 5 in the same list. The main paper validates PKM2 and WWP1, not either Hsp90 paralog, and the table provides no peptide counts or bait-versus-control enrichment values.
Purified ARNT promotes ligand-dependent release of Hsp90 from the AHR-Hsp90-p23 complex and formation of the AHR-ARNT DNA-binding complex.

Human MOP3/ARNTL translated in rabbit reticulocyte lysate was recovered with HSP90-specific antiserum at 71% of the mouse AHR positive-control signal, the strongest MOP-HSP90 recovery in two experiments.
FLAG-ARRB1 bait recovers exact HSP90AA1 prey by AP-MS under nonstimulated conditions and the paper-wide two-peptide/two-experiment filter.
The native immunoadsorption reagent is H1/ASGR1-directed and recovers broad HSP90 in an ASGR1-containing receptor complex; the defined Figure 2 bait is separately ASGR2/H2b.

A CK2-phosphorylated GST fusion of the human ASGR2/H2b cytoplasmic domain recovered an Hsp/immunophilin heterocomplex from HuH-7 cytosol, with Hsp90 verified by immunoblot. Native ASGPR immunoadsorption also recovered Hsp90, and rapamycin or the Trf1 trafficking defect reduced Hsp90 association while decreasing surface receptor without changing total receptor.
Anti-ASS immunoprecipitation from mouse lung recovers generic HSP90 within a NOS/arginine-metabolism multiprotein complex.
ATM phosphorylates Hsp90alpha at T5/T7 after ionizing radiation; nuclear Hsp90alpha phosphorylation correlates with DNA damage-response signaling.

Anti-ATP1A1 co-IP LC-MS/MS in A549 cells recovered an HSP90AA1 protein group containing P07900 in control and LPS conditions (19 unique peptides; spectral counts 27 versus IgG 0 and 23 versus IgG 0; reported fold changes 3.647905 and 3.010210).
Individually expressed ATP6V1A constructs recovered HSP90AA1 in the reported affinity-capture Western experiment.

Corrected full text reports Aurora B interacts with and requires the Cdc37/Hsp90 complex for stability; Cdc37 co-immunoprecipitates with Aurora B and Hsp90 in mammalian and Drosophila extracts, and geldanamycin disrupts the association in some cell contexts.
AXIN1 co-immunoprecipitates with broad cytosolic HSP90 in a Wnt-regulatory complex.

Taipale 2012 classifies AXL as a strong HSP90 kinase client, with Hsp90 interaction score 3.88, dissociation after ganetespib -2.06, protein level after ganetespib 0.52, Hsp90 luminescence 2.972606, and Cdc37 luminescence 3.810154. This is strong broad HSP90/Cdc37 AXL client-screen support, but the workbook does not separate HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1.
In silico T2D/Mpox common-gene/PPI/docking study; HSP90AA1 is a co-hub, not mechanistic HSP90 evidence for ASS1/B2M/HADHA.

BAG2 localizes with and binds misfolded mutant p53 aggregates, promotes aggregate formation, and recruits HSP90 to maintain aggregate propagation; BAG2 silencing or IPI-504 reduces aggregates and increases chemotherapy sensitivity.
An Alzheimer brain proteomic reanalysis reports decreases of HSP90 paralogs and increased BAG3 in affected tissue; Figure 7 proposes an HSF1-linked response.
BAG4 reciprocally co-immunoprecipitates with HSP90/Hsc70 in liver-derived cells and modulates the Hsc70 ATPase/editosome context.

BAG6 is an exact normalized-intensity secretome hit after HSP90AA1 knockout (source row 232; KO/EV=0.382007545430069; log2 fold change=-1.388326960168136; P=0.0072164618535586; q=0.0362544686234868; decreased_in_ko).

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-BAP1 screen record. BAP1 affinity capture -> HSP90AB1: score 7685, 71 significant sequences, emPAI 45.96. No control column or HSP90-specific validation; AP-MS screen support only.

The source supports PKM2 as an HSP90AA1/HSP90alpha1 client-like conformational substrate under oxidative stress. HSP90alpha1 interacts with PKM2, recombinant HSP90alpha1 WT but not ATPase-dead G97D exposes a PKM2 epitope and enables PKM2-Bcl2 binding, and HSP90alpha1 WT rescue supports Bcl2 stability. BCL2 is downstream, stabilized by PKM2-dependent T69 phosphorylation that blocks Cul3-Rbx1 recruitment; CUL3 is the downstream E3 ligase axis rather than an HSP90 interactor.
BCL6 associates with HSP90, and chemically distinct HSP90 inhibitors destabilize BCL6 and suppress BCL6-dependent lymphoma phenotypes.

The inspected open PMC text reports endogenous HSP90alpha-BCLAF1 co-IP in HCC cells and tumor tissue, HSP90AA1 knockdown/KO reducing BCLAF1 protein without lowering BCLAF1 mRNA, HSP90beta knockdown not affecting BCLAF1, HSP90alpha MD-CTD domain association, novobiocin-driven BCLAF1 loss, MG132 rescue, BCLAF1 ubiquitination, and CHX-compatible degradation behavior.

p210 BCR-ABL co-immunoprecipitates with HSP90 and p23; geldanamycin changes its chaperone complex, reduces protein abundance, and proteasome inhibitors protect it, supporting a fusion-product HSP90 client relationship.

Full text reports Hsp90 forms a complex with Beclin 1 through an evolutionarily conserved domain, maintains Beclin 1 stability, and geldanamycin promotes proteasomal Beclin 1 degradation while inhibiting TLR-mediated autophagy.

Recombinant survivin/BIRC5 associated with endogenous Hsp90 in rabbit reticulocyte lysate, while a survivin-derived peptide bound the Hsp90 N-terminal pocket in surface-plasmon-resonance and affinity experiments. Shepherdin disrupted the complex and reduced survivin abundance, but the Hsp90 isoform and the specificity of peptide-mediated client effects were unresolved.
Quantitative AP-MS contains exact HSP90AA1 complex edges for seven kinase candidates across KRAS-defined colorectal cell states.

Four chemically distinct Hsp90 inhibitors altered circadian reporter rhythms, and 17-AEP-GA lowered endogenous BMAL1 abundance and shortened endogenous and cMyc-tagged BMAL1 half-lives. Simultaneous Hsp90aa1/Hsp90ab1 siRNA lowered BMAL1 nearly as strongly as Bmal1 siRNA, whereas Hsp90b1 depletion had no comparable effect and the tested low-dose Trap1 siRNA did not lower BMAL1. These results support cytosolic Hsp90-dependent BMAL1 stability and a strong candidate-client relationship, but the authors could not detect a BMAL1-Hsp90 association and explicitly retained possible indirect mechanisms.
17-DMAG decreases BMI1 RNA and protein in breast cancer mammospheres; BMI1 immunoprecipitation does not recover HSP90alpha, and EZH2/c-Myc mediate BMI1 expression changes.
Quantitative AP-MS contains exact HSP90AA1 complex edges for seven kinase candidates across KRAS-defined colorectal cell states.
Anti-HSP90 immunoprecipitation recovers BPIFB4 in a mutation- and PERK-sensitive complex, while HSP90 inhibition blunts BPIFB4-associated vascular/eNOS effects; the antibody is generic HSP90.

V600E and related activating B-Raf mutants, unlike wild-type B-Raf, associate with Hsp90-Cdc37, lose activity and protein abundance after 17-AAG exposure, undergo proteasome-dependent degradation, and show inhibitor-responsive xenograft growth.

Mutant BRCA1 in rucaparib-resistant clones is stabilized, reciprocally co-IPs with broad HSP90, decreases after 17-DMAG, and HSP90 inhibition restores drug sensitivity, supporting mutant-BRCA1 HSP90 client/stability evidence.

Ganetespib reduced BRCA2 and RAD51 abundance in MCF7 cells in dose- and time-dependent experiments, lowered both proteins in nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions, reduced irradiation-induced RAD51 foci, and depleted BRCA2 and RAD51 in MCF7 xenografts; the associated homologous-recombination defect sensitized cells and xenografts to the PARP inhibitor ABT-888.
BRD4 is supported as an Hsp90 client: Brd4 co-IPs endogenous Hsp90, STA9090 lowers BRD4 protein but not mRNA, MG132 rescues the loss, and HSF1 siRNA lowers Hsp90 and Brd4.
BRMS1 is stabilized by broad Hsp90 and undergoes proteasomal degradation when Hsp90 is inhibited.
CD147/BSG associates with HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1, and HSP90 protects CD147 from FBXO6-mediated ubiquitination/degradation in cervical-cancer radioresistance models.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-BTF3 screen record. BTF3 IP-MS -> HSP90AB1: score 166.97, 30% coverage, 19 peptides, 11 unique peptides, 20 spectra. The list is labeled BTF3-specific but exposes no IgG values; no HSP90 validation/client evidence.
The protein is recovered in PU-H71 HSP90 affinity-proteomics networks in cancer cells.
Local BioPlex 3.0 parsed HSP90-edge tables contain C10ORF137 edges to both HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 in both 293T and HCT116, with high pInt values around 0.99998-0.999999.
C1QL1 associates with HSP90alpha and promotes its ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation, with downstream ER-stress/UPR effects.
ANXA2, C9, PDIA3, HSP90AA1, and HSP90AB1 are part of calcific aortic valve disease proteomic and validation context. The source is not direct interaction or client evidence for the queued genes.

Dataset EV1 contains an exact HSP90AA1 row in the C9ORF72-HA affinity-purification mass-spectrometry screen (Btz-versus-DMSO q=0.3434; difference=0.539). The authors' Significant field is blank for this row.
CaV1.2/CACNA1C enters a KIF5B-STIP1-dependent Hsp70-to-broad-Hsp90 transport and quality-control pathway linked to channel stability.

CacyBP/SIP is a cytosolic Hsp90-binding chaperone/cochaperone-machinery regulator: it co-IPs with Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta, maps to Hsp90beta middle-domain-containing constructs, shows PLA and purified-protein ELISA binding, retains binding after Hsp90 inhibitor treatment, has chaperone-like activity, and shifts Hsp90 pI patterns consistent with possible dephosphorylation.

This source supports an HSP90AA1-resolved FBXO7 relationship in ccRCC. Fig3 nominates FBXO7 by HSP90AA1 Co-IP/silver-stain/MS, predicts an HSP90AA1-FBXO7 docking model, validates reciprocal exogenous and endogenous co-IP, and shows cytoplasmic coexpression. Fig5 shows HSP90AA1 overexpression increases FBXO7 protein, HSP90AA1 knockdown decreases FBXO7 protein, FBXO7 mRNA is unchanged, and MG132 raises FBXO7 while blunting the HSP90AA1-dependent difference. Fig7 places FBXO7 downstream of HSP90AA1 for CADM1/PI3K-AKT pathway readouts.
Primary source inspection supports complex comember evidence for the listed HSP90AA1 routes. The evidence is retained as support only and does not establish client biology.
CAMKMT binds the Hsp90 middle domain, yields isoform-distinguishing HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 peptides, and decreases after geldanamycin treatment.
CANX/calnexin participates in the RDH5 ER-localization complex whose association is maintained by HSP90alpha and HSP90beta.
The protein is captured in an HSP90-associated network and shows abundance response after HSP90 inhibition.

HSP90 expression correlates with inflammasome components in alcoholic liver disease, and 17-DMAG reduces NLRP3 inflammasome readouts in liver macrophage and BMDM models, partly through HSF1/HSPA1A response.

Radicicol disrupts the inducible HSP90-SRC-CASP8 complex, increases CASP8 ubiquitination, lowers CASP8 abundance when protein synthesis is blocked, and increases CASP8 and CASP3 cleavage; MG132 causes CASP8 accumulation. These results support broad HSP90-dependent candidate-client behavior.

In native human platelets, caveolin-1 was detected after immunoprecipitation of broad Hsp90, NOS3, beta-actin, or caveolin-1, placing Hsp90 and CAV1 in a caveolar multiprotein complex without resolving the Hsp90 isoform.

CBL is support-only ErbB2 degradation-pathway context. The source's HSP90 relationship is ErbB2-Hsp90/Hsp70 chaperone exchange after geldanamycin, while c-Cbl appears in ErbB2 ubiquitination/trafficking context.

Taipale 2014 supports CCDC117 as a strong HSP90-associated direct-assay interactor: AP-MS and LUMIER row 50 records HSP90AB1-CCDC117 with LUMIER 13.217723 and SAINT AvgP 1.0, and LUMIER row 246 shows both HSP90AA1 10.289581 and HSP90AB1 13.217723.

Drosophila Cyclin B affinity purification identifies Hsp83 and Msps, endogenous complexes are recovered reciprocally, and Hsp83 mutation or geldanamycin alters Cyclin B spindle localization; human HeLa cells show a parallel cyclin B localization phenotype after Hsp90 inhibition without loss of total cyclin B.
Celastrol inhibits HSP90 ATPase activity, induces HSP70, reduces cell-cycle proteins, and disrupts HSP90-Cdc37-Cdk complexes in U937 leukemia cells.

Corrected full text reports FKBP4-Hsp90 BioID identifies CCT8, FKBP4 knockdown causes CCT8 aggregation and compromises CCT8 client stability, and the authors describe CCT8 as a client of the FKBP4-Hsp90 complex.

Type III CD38 is supported as a generic-HSP90 folding/stability client candidate in a cytosolic quality-control complex. DNAJA2 is broader Hsc70/Hsp90 machinery and degradation-regulator context rather than an HSP90 client claim.

In human HCT-115 and SW480 colorectal cancer cells, EndoMT conditioned medium increased CD44 mRNA; anti-HSP90alpha antibody or extracellular HSP90 inhibitor antagonized the response. Recombinant HSP90alpha increased CD44 mRNA and cell-surface CD44, with anti-CD91 blocking the mRNA response. This supports a compartment-specific downstream response to extracellular HSP90alpha, not CD44 binding or HSP90 client maturation.
FLAG-CD47 IP-MS identifies mouse Hsp90aa1 and reciprocal exact-HSP90α co-IP validates CD47-HSP90α association in 293T cells and differentiated myotubes.
HSP90AA1 CRISPR knockout lowers cellular and exosome-associated CD63 abundance in MDA-MB-231 cells while measured exosome particle size and output remain similar.
B-cell-receptor components reciprocally associate with HSP90 and show abundance changes after HSP90 inhibition or knockdown in leukemia cells.

LC-MS/MS identifies HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 as enriched in exosomes from ER-stressed HepG2 cells, and a generic HSP90 immunoblot validates exosomal abundance. Stable HSP90 shRNA in donor tumor cells reduces exosomal HSP90 and weakens recipient dendritic-cell CD80 induction and antitumor function. CD80 is therefore a downstream maturation readout of exosomal cytosolic Hsp90 signaling, not a direct partner or client.

CD81 is an exact whole_cell_proteome response after HSP90AA1 knockout (source row 3166; KO/EV=0.264518046620901; log2 fold change=-1.9185619419910884; P=0.0010560367875093; q=0.0321684155330831; decreased_in_ko). Matched GSE208005 descriptive RNA direction is decreased_in_ko.

Supplementary Table S2 lists NCBI accession 153792590, heat shock protein HSP 90-alpha isoform 1, among 21 proteins identified after FLAG-CD9 affinity capture and mass spectrometry in glioma stem cells.
Geldanamycin causes CDC25A degradation and accelerates heat-shock-induced loss, supporting Hsp90-dependent protection of CDC25A abundance.

Endogenous CDC25C coimmunoprecipitated with broad Hsp90 in A172 cells, CDC25C protein declined after geldanamycin or 17-AAG without a commensurate mRNA decrease, and three calpain inhibitors partially rescued its loss. Hsp90 inhibition remodeled the CDC25C complex from CDC37 toward Hsp70 and accompanied reduced CDK1 activity and G2/M arrest.

In cardiomyocytes, Hsp90alpha, Hsp90beta, and CDC37 occur in dominant-negative p38alpha/MAPK14 complexes. Recombinant assays show CDC37-assisted recruitment of p38alpha into Hsp90 complexes and suppression of p38alpha autophosphorylation. Hsp90 inhibition or CDC37 knockdown activates p38 signaling; CDC37 overexpression attenuates TAB1beta-induced activation. The study does not establish a TAB1-HSP90 interaction.
Harc/CDC37L1 binds Hsp90, maps a Hsp90-binding domain related to CDC37, and forms complexes with Hsp90, Hsp70, Hop, and immunophilins but not p23.
P07900 HSP1 90kDa protein alpha is marked (2), meaning detected in both anti-CDC5L and anti-SKIP affinity purifications.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-CDC73 screen record. CDC73-eGFP bait -> HSP90B1/endoplasmin: Mascot score 389, mass 92,696, coverage 33.6; the eGFP control also contains HSP90B1 (score 204, coverage 18.3). This is an exact but background-prone AP-MS row, not validated binding/client evidence.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-CDH5 screen record. miniTurbo-CDH5 whole-cell bait -> HSP90AB1: -log10(p)=2.781, log2 bait/no-biotin difference 2.838, significant +; control LFQ 28.55/28.76, bait LFQ 31.54/31.45, 12 unique peptides. HSP90AA1 is also significant; this is proximity-screen support, not direct binding/client evidence.

Geldanamycin treatment caused progressive loss of CDK1 protein in HeLa and A549 cells, while early CDK1 activity promoted beta-TrCP-dependent ubiquitination and degradation of misfolded PLK1 after HSP90 inhibition. CDK1 siRNA increased PLK1, CDK1 overexpression prolonged PLK1 loss after geldanamycin, and CDK1 enhanced PLK1 ubiquitination in cells and in vitro. The current article therefore places CDK1 as a pharmacologically responsive downstream kinase in an HSP90-controlled degradation pathway, but it does not assay HSP90-CDK1 binding, genetic HSP90 dependence, or isoform scope and should not by itself establish CDK1 as a direct client.

BioPlex contains high-probability AP-MS network edges from CDK11A to HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 in both HEK293T and HCT116, with pInt 0.9923 and 0.9726 in 293T and 0.9902 and 0.9720 in HCT116. This supports repeated cytosolic Hsp90 co-complex/proximity context, not direct binding or client dependence.
CDK11p110 and CDK11p46 associate with broad Hsp90/Cdc37 and require Hsp90 activity for stability and pro-apoptotic function.

Taipale 2012 kinase table classifies CDK15 as Strong with Hsp90 interaction score 5.59, ganetespib dissociation -3.06, protein level after ganetespib 0.23, localization 'unknown', and CDC37 luminescence 7.040186.

Nascent CDK2 assembles with endogenous HSP90 and CDC37 in rabbit reticulocyte lysate, geldanamycin during synthesis prevents the salt-stable complex, and geldanamycin lowers endogenous CDK2 in K562 cells.

Taipale 2012 kinase table classifies CDK3 as a weak Hsp90 kinase client with Hsp90 interaction score 2.58, ganetespib dissociation -0.79, protein level after ganetespib 0.51, and CDC37 luminescence support.

CDC37 overexpression increases CDK4 abundance, half-life, and CDK4-HSP90 association; CDC37 mutants that reduce HSP90 binding still support kinase-client chaperoning, separating CDC37-client loading from simple CDC37-HSP90 tethering.
Exact bait-prey row retained in MERGED, CeMM-only, ETHZ-only; seqcov.max=0.55, pc_sup.max=19, sc.max=77, wSC merged/CeMM/ETHZ=218.709 / 131 / 106.

FNIP1 is supported as an Hsp90 co-chaperone/chaperone-cycle regulator. FNIP1, FNIP2, and Tsc1 act as specialized Hsp90 co-chaperones/chaperone-cycle regulators: F1/F2 map Hsp90alpha-associated co-IP/domain interactions and FNIP/Tsc1 complex architecture, while F3/F4 show these co-chaperone combinations tune Hsp90alpha-dependent client activity and steroid hormone receptor ligand responsiveness.

Hsp90 inhibition and altered cochaperone dosage changed Matrin3 toxicity, inclusion formation, and stress sensitivity in yeast and neuronal models.

In mutant-TP53 tumor cells, MDM2 immunoprecipitation recovered Hsp90alpha, and the paper explicitly showed that this association was absent without mutant p53 and therefore indirect and mutant-p53-bridged. Radicicol or geldanamycin disrupted the ternary complex, increased MDM2 ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover, restored MDM2-ARF association and nucleolar localization, and enabled MDM2-dependent mutant-p53 degradation. Antibody-epitope interference suggests close Hsp90 contact with the central MDM2 region but does not establish purified direct binding. MDM2 is therefore an HSP90AA1-containing complex member and downstream regulated E3 ligase, not an Hsp90 client demonstrated by pairwise binding or folding dependence.

MLKL is the actual HSP90 source object in this article. Multiple HSP90 inhibitors block MLKL-driven necroptosis downstream of RIPK3 activation, HSP90 inhibition prevents MLKL oligomerisation and membrane translocation, Cdc37 knockdown reduces activated MLKL-mediated death, and MLKL transiently co-fractionates/co-IPs with HSP90/Cdc37. AF9/MLLT3 directly associates with an HSP90-HSP70-HOP complex; HSP90 knockdown or novobiocin redistributes AF9 and changes AF9-regulated transcription.
Recombinant human MMP14 cleaves purified HSP90alpha in vitro in a membrane-protein shedding study.

Cell-based iTRAQ degradomics identified extracellular HSP90alpha, but not HSP90beta, as selectively altered with active MMP2, and purified active MMP2 directly cleaved HSP90alpha into approximately 80-kDa and 50-kDa fragments before clearance.

The synthetic HSP90 inhibitor PF4942847 reduced MMP9 gelatinase activity and MMP9 protein in HOS-MNNG osteosarcoma cells while suppressing migration, invasion, angiogenesis, and pulmonary metastases. The current results therefore support MMP9 as a downstream HSP90-regulated effector in this pharmacologic osteosarcoma context, not as a demonstrated HSP90 client or physical binding partner.
MOB3C result matrices contain exact HSP90AA1 rows in the MOB3C affinity/proximity experiments.

MRE11 directly binds PIH1D1 and is R2TP-regulated; HSP90 involvement is through R2TP, not direct HSP90-MRE11 binding.

MTHFD1 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.

These current experiments support a functional Hsp90-eNOS complex and regulation of eNOS activity, not a classical folding or stability client claim.

The Results explicitly state that NUAK2 associated with the Cdc37-Hsp90 chaperone heterodimer.

NUDC is supported as an HSP90alpha-linked cochaperone or chaperone-cycle regulator. NudC binds Hsp90alpha and LIS1, forms endogenous biochemical complexes with LIS1/Hsp90, Hsp90 inhibitors reduce LIS1 stability, Hsp90 overexpression partially rescues LIS1 loss caused by NudC-L279P, and purified NudC modulates Hsp90 ATPase activity.

Taipale 2014 LUMIER reports NUDCD1 with HSP90AA1 score -1.254761, HSP90AB1 score -0.732977, CDC37 -1.332423, and selected cochaperone signals; this is direct-assay association context, not client mechanism.

RCC2 is strong generic-HSP90/NudCL2 stability evidence. NudCL2 forms a complex with Hsp90 to stabilize RCC2 at the midbody, and the queued NUDC term should be treated as a paralog/name-family ambiguity rather than evidence for NUDC itself.
Primary source inspection supports complex comember evidence for the listed HSP90AA1 routes. The evidence is retained as support only and does not establish client biology.
NUFIP1 is an indirect R2TP-associated Hsp90 assembly cofactor/scaffold, not an Hsp90 client or demonstrated direct binder.
NUMA1 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.
NUP62 and other MAb414-reactive nucleoporins co-immunoprecipitate with broad Hsp90 machinery, and NUP62 binding to chaperoned glucocorticoid receptor is enhanced in reconstituted transport assays.
Supplementary Figure 7 independently recovers broad Hsp90 in FLAG-NWD1 immunoprecipitates.
Full-length nucleocytoplasmic OGT is a broad cytosolic-Hsp90 client.
GST-ORP2 pull-downs from HuH7 lysates contained endogenous CDC37, Hsp90, and active AKT, and ORP2 depletion reduced AKT signaling, supporting ORP2 membership in an Hsp90-CDC37-AKT regulatory complex.
HSP90AA1/P07900;43 peptides;normalized means control=8.34418e-4,WT=9.35020e-4,N22A=2.32487e-3;N22A/control=2.786,p=0.00533;N22A/WT=2.486,p=0.00605;WT/control=1.121,p=0.717
The cited source resolves HSP90AA1 in the OVOL2-centered Affinity Capture-MS result.

HSP90 inhibitor geldanamycin blocks ATP/P2X7R-mediated IL-1 beta release and reduces endogenous NLRP3 protein, supporting HSP90-dependent NLRP3 inflammasome stability/function in salivary epithelial cells.

The queued genes and HSP90 family members occur in a tumor proteostasis abundance signature. The source does not support direct HSP90 interactions or client relationships for HSPA1B, HSPA9, P4HB, TXN, or VCP.

Supplementary Table S4 identifies HSP90AA1 (P07900) in FLAG-USP52/PAN2 immunoprecipitates with protein score 70, three peptides, three unique peptides, and 4.8% coverage. The matched uninduced control columns contain not-applicable placeholders, consistent with the article's exclusion of control-only proteins. This reproduces the exact database route at an affinity-purification MS screen ceiling.

PARK7/DJ-1 affinity purification from in vivo cross-linked mouse tissues and ES cells identifies Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperone-network proteins as DJ-1 candidate interactors. Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta are selectively coenriched with DJ-1 in ES-cell datasets, and DJ-1 knockout ES cells show reduced levels of Hsp90 client proteins Raf-1 and Akt, while geldanamycin does not deplete DJ-1.

PCDH7-BirA proximity labeling with streptavidin enrichment and LC-MS/MS identified significant interphase and mitotic proximal proteins across four biological replicates at FDR 0.05. Main Figure 3A visibly labels HSP90AA1, HSP90AB1, and HSP90B1 as nodes in the PCDH7 proximity network, directly resolving all three queued source routes at the screen level. The study performs targeted PLA, co-immunoprecipitation, and functional follow-up only for ZDHHC5, so the HSP90-family results remain proximity-screen association rather than direct binding, client, or functional-dependence evidence.

PCGF6 appears in multiple Taipale 2012 workbook rows. The E3 ligase row 109 has Hsp90 interaction 0.72 and an Hsp90 interactor flag, while the other E3/transcription-factor rows are lower or unflagged. This supports broad HSP90 candidate-client/direct-assay context, but duplicate/construct heterogeneity and lack of alpha/beta comparison prevent isoform-specific or validated-client interpretation.

Taipale 2014 LUMIER reports PDCD5 with HSP90AA1 score 0.063749, HSP90AB1 score -0.238462, CDC37 0.314508, and selected cochaperone signals; this is direct-assay association context, not client mechanism.

PDGFRA associates with cytosolic Hsp90 and CDC37 in cancer-cell contexts; separate HSP90alpha and HSP90beta siRNAs reduce PDGFRA, and Hsp90 inhibition promotes receptor ubiquitination, proteasome-dependent loss, altered localization/conformation, and reduced growth.
ANXA2, C9, PDIA3, HSP90AA1, and HSP90AB1 are part of calcific aortic valve disease proteomic and validation context. The source is not direct interaction or client evidence for the queued genes.
PDIA4 associates with broad HSP90 by IP-MS, co-IP, colocalization, and recombinant pull-down; PDIA4 helps stabilize MYC in the proposed axis.
Taipale 2012 kinase table classifies PDIK1L/CLIK1L as a weak Hsp90 kinase client with Hsp90 interaction score 2.74 and ganetespib dissociation -2.30, but protein level after ganetespib is 0.86.

PDK1 coimmunoprecipitated with Hsp90, Hsp90 inhibition disrupted the complex and destabilized PDK1 through a partly proteasome-dependent route, Hsp90 overexpression enhanced PDK1-Src assembly and PDK1 activity, and Hsp90 knockdown reduced PDK1 activity and Src binding.
HSP90alpha and HSP90beta are nominated as PER2 partners; co-IP/GST pulldown and PAS1-domain mapping support PER2-HSP90 binding that competes with the HSP90-IKK complex.
PFAS associates with HSP90-chaperone machinery in LUMIER and purinosome-localization experiments.

PFKFB3 affinity-purification/mass-spectrometry discovery identified both HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 in main Table 2. In separate functional experiments, PFKFB3 knockdown reduced CDK4 recovery with the endogenous Hsp90-Cdc37 complex, whereas wild-type PFKFB3, but not the CDK4-binding-deficient K147A mutant, supported CDK4 association with that complex and CDK4 protein stability. These results support PFKFB3 association with and regulation of a shared cytosolic Hsp90-containing complex, but they do not establish direct PFKFB3-Hsp90 binding or an Hsp90-client relationship.

Taipale 2014 LUMIER reports PFKP with HSP90AA1 score 0.385835, HSP90AB1 score -0.270562, CDC37 0.076638, and selected cochaperone signals; this is direct-assay association context, not client mechanism.

PGAM2 directly interacts with HSP90AA1, referred to as HSP90 in the work, and stabilizes it in Ang II-induced cardiac hypertrophy models. Co-IP/PLA and residue-mapping support PGAM2-HSP90 interaction, PGAM2 knockdown lowers HSP90 protein without lowering transcript, CHX/ubiquitination assays support HSP90 turnover regulation, and HSP90 restoration rescues downstream mTOR/IKKalpha signaling.

This source supports PGK1 as a recruiter co-chaperone/direct HSP90alpha C-domain binding adapter for the GSK3beta client. GSK3beta IP/MS nominated PGK1, reciprocal co-IP and clinical breast-cancer tissue IP show Hsp90-PGK1-GSK3beta complexes, PGK1 knockdown reduces GSK3beta and Hsp90-GSK3beta binding, purified His-PGK1 directly binds GST-C-Hsp90alpha, and PGK1 enables GSK3beta association with C-terminal Hsp90alpha. 17-AAG disrupts PGK1 binding to closed-state Hsp90alpha and the Hsp90alpha-PGK1-GSK3beta complex.

The main paper explicitly reports broad HSP90 in a controlled PGR co-complex screen, but does not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1. IntAct routes describe tagged PGR co-IP/SILAC, but the v6.170 archive contains only excluded article images and no quantitative supplement table or candidate row.
PI4K2A proximity-labeling/IP-MS identifies HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1, and PI4K2A loss disrupts HSP90 recruitment to AXL and AXL stability.
PI4K2B is recovered with Hsp90alpha, co-immunoprecipitates with tagged alpha and endogenous Hsp90, and loses stability, localization, and activity when the Hsp90 interaction is disrupted.
Interaction screens identify both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta with PIDD, and broad-Hsp90/p23 validation establishes an Hsp90-dependent PIDD stability and function mechanism.
Structural work maps RPAP3 TPR2 binding to HSP90 C-terminal tail, RPAP3/PIH1D1 complex architecture, and a human R2T/R2TP model for HSP90 recruitment and activation.
B-cell-receptor components reciprocally associate with HSP90 and show abundance changes after HSP90 inhibition or knockdown in leukemia cells.
Geldanamycin accelerates PIM1 loss and reduces kinase activity, supporting a cytosolic-HSP90 client mechanism.

PINK1-FLAG affinity purification/MS and co-IP recover both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta with CDC37; geldanamycin destabilizes PINK1 forms and the HSP90/CDC37 system changes PINK1 maturation and subcellular distribution.

Taipale 2014 LUMIER reports PITPNB with HSP90AA1 score 0.046217, HSP90AB1 score 0.217599, CDC37 -0.68931, and selected cochaperone signals; this is direct-assay association context, not client mechanism.

Full-text review confirms PIWIL4 IP-MS/co-IP evidence for PIWIL4-HSP90AA1 binding and shows that the piR-31115-PIWIL4 complex protects HSP90AA1 from ubiquitination/degradation in MDA-MB-231 cells; HSP90AA1 knockdown attenuates the migration phenotype. This is HSP90AA1-resolved upstream-stabilization/direct-partner evidence for PIWIL4, not evidence that PIWIL4 is an HSP90 client.

The inspected source supports PKM2, encoded by PKM, as the actual HSP90-regulated protein: HSP90 binds PKM2 by AP-MS/co-IP/GST pulldown, HSP90 knockdown or inhibitors reduce PKM2 abundance, proteasome blockade rescues PKM2, and HSP90-GSK3beta-dependent Thr-328 phosphorylation stabilizes PKM2 and supports HCC glycolysis/growth phenotypes.

The source supports PKM2 as an HSP90AA1/HSP90alpha1 client-like conformational substrate under oxidative stress. HSP90alpha1 interacts with PKM2, recombinant HSP90alpha1 WT but not ATPase-dead G97D exposes a PKM2 epitope and enables PKM2-Bcl2 binding, and HSP90alpha1 WT rescue supports Bcl2 stability. BCL2 is downstream, stabilized by PKM2-dependent T69 phosphorylation that blocks Cul3-Rbx1 recruitment; CUL3 is the downstream E3 ligase axis rather than an HSP90 interactor.

Taipale 2012 kinase table classifies PKN1 as Weak with Hsp90 interaction score 2.63, ganetespib dissociation -2.66, protein level after ganetespib 1.19, localization 'Cytoplasm', and CDC37 luminescence 4.513255.
Extracellular Hsp90alpha associates with and stabilizes secreted uPA in elastin-peptide-stimulated fibrosarcoma cells, supporting migration and invasion.
B-cell-receptor components reciprocally associate with HSP90 and show abundance changes after HSP90 inhibition or knockdown in leukemia cells.
Secreted HSP90alpha promotes extracellular plasminogen activation and plasmin-dependent migration; the physical co-IP/MS partner in the same complex is tPA/PLAT, not PLG.

Lipid-droplet proteomics identified HSP90A, explicitly defined as the HSP90AA1 product. HSP90A and PLIN2 reciprocally co-immunoprecipitated, oleic acid increased their lipid-droplet association, and HSP90A knockdown stabilized PLIN2 without changing its transcript; lysosomal inhibition and LAMP2A experiments placed HSP90A in PLIN2 lysosomal degradation.

The PLK2/PLK3 substrate-recognition study and supplements include HSP90 and GRP94/HSP90B1 phosphosites/substrate context, supporting PLK2/PLK3 as upstream kinase-substrate context for HSP90-family proteins rather than a queued generic GRP gene claim.
PLK3 associates with broad HSP90 and promotes its proteasomal degradation, reducing HSP90-dependent STAT3/HK2 signaling.

The zinc-inducible PML/RARA fusion reduced HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 transcripts and broad HSP90 protein in U937-PR9 cells but not zinc-treated mock controls. In PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, anti-PML chromatin immunoprecipitation recovered defined HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 promoter regions; ATRA-mediated fusion degradation reduced promoter occupancy, increased H3K14 acetylation, and restored HSP90 transcription. This supports a fusion-specific PML-component upstream transcriptional-regulator relationship for both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms, not an HSP90 client or isolated wild-type PML mechanism.

PNCK is supported as a shared cytosolic HSP90 client-like kinase and HSP90-complex perturbation source. PNCK coimmunoprecipitates with Hsp90, geldanamycin destroys PNCK and enhances EGFR degradation, PNCK-induced EGFR degradation coincides with proteasomal PNCK loss, and Hsp90 alpha/beta phosphorylation changes are detected by mass spectrometry.

GFP-Pol eta co-immunoprecipitated separately detected Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta, while reciprocal endogenous co-IP supported an Hsp90-Pol eta complex. Hsp90 inhibition reduced Pol eta abundance, shortened its half-life, promoted proteasome-sensitive loss, impaired UV-induced nuclear-focus accumulation, and reduced interaction with ubiquitinated PCNA; the text also reports alpha/beta RNAi effects in supplemental Figure S3D.
HSP90 and the R2TP/prefoldin-like machinery bind unassembled RNA polymerase II subunits and support cytoplasmic POLR2A/RPB1 assembly and stability.
HSP90AA1-TAP proteomics identifies EDRF1, MYLK2, and POLR2E in nucleotide- or geldanamycin-conditioned HSP90alpha complexes.

Supplementary Table 2 lists P07900 HSP90 among Oct-1/POU2F1-interacting proteins identified by co-IP and MS (score 20.91, 7.51% coverage, 84.6 kDa). This is exact HSP90AA1 screen support without pairwise validation.
PPARA co-immunoprecipitates with Hsp90 and XAP2, and mammalian two-hybrid/domain assays map Hsp90 association to the PPARA E/F region.

The pan-HSP90 inhibitor 17-AAG reduces EGF-supported PPARδ protein accumulation, diminishes HSP90 recovery with immunoprecipitated PPARδ, and suppresses PPARδ-driven GLUT1 and SLC1A5 reporter activity, providing broad inhibitor-linked candidate-client and downstream functional support.
PPARG is negative in the HSP90alpha-fragment and mammalian two-hybrid assays; small reporter changes under broad perturbations provide context but not a physical or client relationship.
Purified GST-CyP40 binds recombinant human Hsp90alpha in a reconstituted pulldown and competes with S100A1 or S100A2, while cellular co-IP confirms Hsp90 association.
Local PDF reports a source-era CYC4/CRN complex mapping to PPIL2/CRNKL1 in chaperone interaction context with Hsp90/Hsp70; evidence is nomenclature-caveated complex support, not client evidence.

Taipale 2014 LUMIER reports PPP1R7 with HSP90AA1 score 5.28615, HSP90AB1 score 3.001246, CDC37 0.334905, and selected cochaperone signals; this is direct-assay association context, not client mechanism.
HSP90alpha associates with PPP3CA/calcineurin in the DRP1 dephosphorylation complex.

The article directly tests PP5/Hsp90 binding competition and PP5 activation by Hsp90/HspC90. It supports PPP5C/PP5 as a direct Hsp90-binding phosphatase partner with regulatory activation context, not as an Hsp90 client.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-PPT1 screen record. CTAP-PPT1 bait -> HSP90AA1: bait spectra 8|10|20, controls 4|0|0, SAINT probability 0.98, fold change 9.5, BFDR 0.01. Strong screen-level enrichment, not validated binding/client evidence.

Taipale 2014 LUMIER reports PRDM1 with HSP90AA1 score 6.443587, HSP90AB1 score 7.521851, CDC37 3.368831, and selected cochaperone signals; this is direct-assay association context, not client mechanism.
HSP90alpha was identified with PRDM14, validated by isoform-named co-IP, purified-protein SPR and live-cell NanoBRET, with C-terminal PRDM14 dependence.

Taipale 2012 classifies PRKAA1/AMPK alpha1 row 28 as a strong HSP90 kinase-client screen hit with Hsp90 interaction score 4.89, ganetespib dissociation -2.5, protein level after ganetespib 0.14, and Cdc37 luminescence 5.188177. A second PRKAA1 construct row 216 is Non and has Hsp90 interaction score 0.
Exact bait-prey row retained in MERGED, CeMM-only, ETHZ-only; seqcov.max=0.42, pc_sup.max=15, sc.max=52, wSC merged/CeMM/ETHZ=122.665 / 77 / 56.

PRKACB is classified as a strong kinase client in the Taipale 2012 workbook, with Hsp90 interaction score 5.59, Cdc37 luminescence 7.783075, ganetespib-associated dissociation -3.41, and protein level after ganetespib 0.47. This supports broad cytosolic HSP90/Cdc37 kinase-client biology but not HSP90AB1 specificity.
Repeated source statements support PKC-alpha recovery with generic HSP90 and celastrol-sensitive co-complex association.
PRKCD is present in the broad HSP90-associated Fc-epsilon receptor signaling complex and responds to celastrol treatment.
Broad HSP90alpha/beta co-immunoprecipitates with PRKCE during ischemia/reperfusion and Hsp90 inhibition or an interaction-site peptide impairs PRKCE mitochondrial import and cardioprotection.
Quantitative AP-MS contains exact HSP90AA1 complex edges for seven kinase candidates across KRAS-defined colorectal cell states.

Flag-PKCz affinity proteomics in MDA-MB-231 cells reports IPI00784295.2, HSP90AA1, as Isoform 1 of heat shock protein HSP 90-alpha in Additional file 1 Table S1; the pair was not selected for orthogonal validation.
The protein is captured in an HSP90-associated network and shows abundance response after HSP90 inhibition.
PRKD3 associates with HSP90 and undergoes inhibitor-linked, proteasome-dependent loss, supporting HSP90-dependent stability.
A partially purified human HeLa dsDNA-activated kinase phosphorylates HSP90alpha, but not HSP90beta, at two amino-terminal threonines in vitro.
Parkin tandem-affinity proteomics recovers HSP90AA1 together with other HSP90-family members; the gene is normalized from PARK2 to PRKN.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-PRMT1 screen record. FLAG-PRMT1 bait -> HSP90AB1: spectral counts 22|21|1 versus vector 8|9|0. Exact AP-MS row with appreciable control recovery; no direct/client validation.
Mechanistic association,mutant,and methyl-peptide evidence supports PRMT5 as an upstream regulator of HSP90AA1;it does not establish purified binary binding or PRMT5 client dependence on HSP90AA1.

Anti-PrP immunoprecipitation from wild-type but not PRNP-null human melanoma cells followed by gel-band MS identified a Table 2 entry labeled only Heat shock protein HSP 90; no accession, alpha/beta label, peptide count, or Hsp90-specific validation is provided.
Protein C stimulation promotes PROCR-tail association with HSP90AA1; AP-MS and western validation support a PROCR-HSP90AA1-SRC-IGF1R plasma-membrane signaling complex in mammary stem cells.
PRPF31 appears in a related U4/PAQosome proteomic context, but the manuscript states its route to R2TP is unclear and does not establish PRPF31 as an HSP90 client or interactor.
HSP90/R2TP binds unassembled PRPF8 and SNRNP200, protects them from loss, and promotes U5 snRNP assembly.

HSP90AA1 is a source-defined Virotrap candidate interactor for the listed PRPSAP1_FL_and_PR_both_exact_in_source_row;record_specific_FL_PR_crosswalk_not_published condition set at bait-versus-eDHFR FDR <= 0.01;this is VLP co-packaging, not binary binding or client evidence.
Table S2B row 864 P07900/HSP90AA1 K585 KVEKVVVSNR to Q9Y520/PRRC2C K571 QKEKEK; both groups are accession-resolved.

PRSS8 is an exact secretome response after HSP90AA1 knockout (source row 101; KO/EV=0.26489204469169; log2 fold change=-1.9165235779302512; P=0.000904057859703; q=0.0104487891060406; decreased_in_ko).

HSP90AA1 is a source-defined Virotrap candidate interactor for the listed PRUNE1_PR_only condition set at bait-versus-eDHFR FDR <= 0.01;this is VLP co-packaging, not binary binding or client evidence.
PSAT1 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.

PSKH2 is a strong kinase-client screen hit in Taipale 2012, with Hsp90 interaction score 5.99, Cdc37 signal 7.151922, protein level after ganetespib 0.11, and Hsp90 dissociation after ganetespib -3.28 in the workbook. This supports broad cytosolic HSP90/Cdc37 kinase-client evidence, not alpha/beta-specific biology.
Sepia high-temperature transcriptome/PPI places PSMA5 near HSP90AA1 hub context only; no direct PSMA5-HSP90 experiment.
PSMB5 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.
The retained source text did not contain a usable passage for this finding. Review the linked paper, limitations, and caveats before interpreting the relationship.
PSMD1 is identified in the endogenous HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation/MS Table 1. The antibody recognizes both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta, so this is shared-cytosolic co-complex evidence only.

PSMD14 co-IP/MS lists HSP90AA1 in Supplementary Table S1, and HSP90AA1 is visibly included in the Figure 3E high-confidence interaction network. No HSP90AA1-specific co-IP or western blot follows; only IMPDH2 is validated, and Table S1 gives no accession, peptide count, score, or control-enrichment metric.
PSMD2 is a proteasome-related diet-response protein; HSP90 is part of broader chaperone/stress-response interpretation without a tested PSMD2-HSP90 relationship.

Supplementary Table 1 resolves exact HSP90AA1 in the RR (Rpn10/PSMD4-Rpn11) cross-link-assisted dual-bait proteasome sample: P07900 is recovered in all four LC-MS/MS runs across two biological replicates.
PTEN is maintained downstream of the PRMT5-HSP90A methylation axis and responds to pan-Hsp90 inhibition,but the source does not show HSP90AA1-PTEN binding or establish PTEN as an HSP90AA1 client.

Tagged and endogenous broad-Hsp90 immunoblots show that PTGDR/DP1 enters an L-PGDS-dependent Hsp90 complex and that the Hsp90 MEEVD motif and L-PGDS W43/G47 surface support the complex. Geldanamycin reduces L-PGDS-promoted DP1 surface export, but no alpha-specific reagent is documented for this cellular route.

Purified full-length His-Hsp90-alpha, catalog 10202, directly retains purified L-PGDS in a reconstituted pull-down. Cellular MEEVD deletion and L-PGDS W43A/G47A mutation provide orthogonal broad-Hsp90 interface support, and the authors explicitly argue L-PGDS is cochaperone-like rather than an Hsp90 client.

Taipale workbook supports PTGES3/p23 as an HSP90-associated cochaperone/source interactor: AP-MS/LUMIER row 49 records HSP90AB1-PTGES3 with LUMIER 15.613533 and SAINT AvgP 0.95, and LUMIER row 434 compares HSP90AB1 15.613533 versus HSP90AA1 7.60265 with beta-leaning centered difference. This is cochaperone/direct-assay evidence, not client evidence.
PGIS/PTGIS co-immunoprecipitates with broad Hsp90 in a vascular prostanoid-synthesis complex whose output changes with agonist and geldanamycin treatment.
COX-2/PTGS2 binds HSP90 and is destabilized through ubiquitin-proteasome mechanisms when the interaction is disrupted; a combined HSP90 alpha/beta siRNA reagent supports cytosolic-Hsp90 dependence.

This source identifies HSP90AA1, PTK2B, and ANXA2 as AD entorhinal-cortex proteins of interest from proteomics/pathway analysis. HSP90AA1 and PTK2B are reported as downregulated DEPs and ANXA2 as an upregulated DEP, then validated by western blot trends and IF/confocal localization with neurons/glia and Abeta/tau pathology. The manuscript does not test HSP90AA1 binding to ANXA2 or PTK2B, nor HSP90-dependent client/stability regulation of either protein.

Geldanamycin shortens PTK6 half-life and promotes proteasome-dependent polyubiquitination in transfected and endogenous breast cancer models. CHIP depletion or knockout blunts PTK6 loss, and inhibitor treatment shifts PTK6 from an Hsp90-Cdc37 complex toward Hsp70-CHIP. These data support broad cytosolic-Hsp90 client biology.
PTPLAD1/hB-ind1 co-immunoprecipitates with broad HA-Hsp90 through an FxxW motif, independently of FKBP8, while FKBP8 strengthens the complex.
B-cell-receptor components reciprocally associate with HSP90 and show abundance changes after HSP90 inhibition or knockdown in leukemia cells.
The cited source resolves HSP90AA1 in the PTPRF-centered Two-hybrid result.
PUS7-bait IP-MS in DLD1 colorectal cancer cells identifies HSP90AA1 with three unique peptides outside the IgG group; generic HSP90 co-IP validates family-level complex association.

HSP90 expression correlates with inflammasome components in alcoholic liver disease, and 17-DMAG reduces NLRP3 inflammasome readouts in liver macrophage and BMDM models, partly through HSF1/HSPA1A response.
Full-length human QRS/QARS and cloned full-length human HSP90alpha produced a strong beta-galactosidase interaction signal in the yeast two-hybrid assay across three independent experiments.
Proteomic discovery and reciprocal HSP90/Rab11a co-IP support HSP90-Rab11a association; colocalization and geldanamycin effects support trafficking context.

Anti-Hsp90alpha affinity purification-mass spectrometry identified RAB11FIP1/RCP with multiple peptides in p53-null and mutant-p53 cells. Reciprocal co-IP, RCP domain mapping, and lysate-based recombinant Hsp90alpha/RCP pulldowns supported an exact alpha-RCP complex.
The protein co-fractionates or co-immunoprecipitates with broad HSP90 in nerve-terminal preparations during toxin-entry experiments.
Aha1 IP-MS recovers RAB3GAP1 and HSP90AA1, and RAB3GAP1 colocalizes with Aha1; Aha1 itself is selectively associated with Hsp90alpha, but pairwise HSP90AA1-RAB3GAP1 binding is not shown.
Rice OsRac1 formed a complex with RAR1, HSP90, and HSP70, and HSP90 inhibition impaired Rac1-dependent innate immune responses.

Anti-Hsp90 immunoprecipitation of MiaPaCa nuclear extracts recovered RAD50 together with MRE11 and NBS1; reciprocal NBS1 immunoprecipitation recovered Hsp90 and RAD50. Hsp90 inhibition impaired RAD50 focus formation but did not reduce RAD50 abundance.

Ganetespib reduced BRCA2 and RAD51 abundance in MCF7 cells in dose- and time-dependent experiments, lowered both proteins in nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions, reduced irradiation-induced RAD51 foci, and depleted BRCA2 and RAD51 in MCF7 xenografts; the associated homologous-recombination defect sensitized cells and xenografts to the PARP inhibitor ABT-888.

RAF1 is classified as a strong kinase client in the Taipale 2012 workbook, with Hsp90 interaction score 5.78, Cdc37 luminescence 8.233346, ganetespib dissociation -2.96, and protein level 0.41 after ganetespib.

Full-text review confirms that HSP90 co-IP from transfected H1299 cells brings down RalBP1, HSF1, and beta-tubulin at 37 C, with stress-responsive dissociation of HSF1 from the RalBP1/HSF1/HSP90/beta-tubulin complex. This supports RALBP1 as a cytosolic HSP90-containing complex member/stress-response context, not direct HSP90-RALBP1 binding and not client evidence.

The zinc-inducible PML/RARA fusion reduced HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 transcripts and broad HSP90 protein in U937-PR9 cells but not zinc-treated mock controls. In PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, fusion occupancy was detected at RARE-containing HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 promoter regions; ATRA-mediated loss of the fusion reduced occupancy, increased H3K14 acetylation, and restored HSP90 transcription. This supports a fusion-specific RARA-component upstream transcriptional-regulator relationship for both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms, not an HSP90 client or isolated wild-type RARA mechanism.
Cdc37 supports CDK4 stability/activity and p-RB1 changes; RB1 is used as a downstream phosphorylation readout in the Cdc37-HSP90-CDK4 pathway.
The FIP200/RB1CC1 differential IP-MS matrix contains exact HSP90AA1 entries.

RCC2 is strong generic-HSP90/NudCL2 stability evidence. NudCL2 forms a complex with Hsp90 to stabilize RCC2 at the midbody, and the queued NUDC term should be treated as a paralog/name-family ambiguity rather than evidence for NUDC itself.

RDH5 is maintained by cytosolic HSP90 in RPE cells: HSP90alpha and HSP90beta associate with RDH5, either isoform loss lowers RDH5 protein without lowering RDH5 mRNA, autophagy/lysosome blockade rescues RDH5, and HSP90 deficiency disrupts RDH5-Calnexin/ER association.

The inspected primary-source table contains the database-routed HSP90AA1-RECQL4 screen record. GFP/FLAG-RECQL4 bait -> HSP90AA1: 23 unique and 71 total peptides, average score/abundance field 2.854. The table has no bait-negative control field; AP-MS support only.

RELA is a downstream NF-kappaB transcription factor branch in this source. The inspected evidence shows FKBP4/Hsp70/RelA interaction and FKBP4-dependent RelA nuclear translocation and NF-kappaB output, not a RELA-Hsp90 interaction or Hsp90 client relationship.
REST binds HSP90alpha in two-hybrid, purified pull-down, and reciprocal endogenous co-IP assays, and HSP90AA1 antisense perturbation changes REST stability/function.

Wild-type RET and multiple MEN2-associated RET mutants were depleted by 17-AAG and radicicol; RET C634R coimmunoprecipitated with endogenous HSP90, 17-AAG reduced that interaction while increasing HSP70 binding, and MG132, ubiquitin, and CHIP experiments demonstrated proteasome-dependent RET polyubiquitination and degradation.
REV1 associates with both Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta and undergoes Hsp90-inhibitor-dependent, proteasome-linked destabilization with reduced mutagenic function.
Recombinant extracellular HSP90alpha increases RhoA activity in 16HBE bronchial epithelial cells whereas matched recombinant beta does not in the reported assay.

Prince 2015 directly tests RHOBTB2/DBC2 binding to HSP90AA1/HSP90alpha and HSP90AB1/HSP90beta in HEK293 overexpression assays. Co-IP shows every HSP90 WT or mutant construct binding RHOBTB2 above pcDNA background, and LUMIER reports greater apparent interaction strength with HSP90alpha than HSP90beta. This is alpha-leaning but shared direct-binding/direct-assay evidence, not alpha-specific biology and not validated RHOBTB2 client-dependence.
The source supports a RHOBTB3-HSP90 relationship but uses generic cytosolic HSP90 language, so it cannot resolve the database-assigned HSP90AA1 paralog.

Human Tom70 directly captures Hsp90 from rabbit reticulocyte lysate and purified bovine Hsp90 through its N-terminal TPR clamp; the R192A clamp mutant abolishes binding. C-terminal Hsp90 competition, geldanamycin, and clamp mutants impair import of selected Tom70-dependent mitochondrial preproteins, supporting Tom70 as a membrane-localized Hsp90/Hsp70 cochaperone.

TOP2A is an exact whole_cell_proteome response after HSP90AA1 knockout (source row 2961; KO/EV=6.98849881464192; log2 fold change=2.8049825864640323; P=0.0001260369402814; q=0.0120688113128691; increased_in_ko). Matched GSE208005 descriptive RNA direction is increased_in_ko. The article independently reports RNA-seq log2FC=0.61 (FDR=3.34e-13), proteome log2FC=2.97 (FDR=0.00917), and Western-blot confirmation in K562, KCL22, and SUP-B15 HSP90alpha-loss models.

TurboID-TOPBP1 bait -> HSP90AA1 abundance record across monolayer/calcium and HPV16 contexts; companion rows contain HSP90AB1/HSP90B1/TRAP1. The table supports proximity-screen detection, not direct binding or client action.

Hsp90 coprecipitated selectively with multiple conformational TP53 core-domain mutants exposing the pAb240 epitope and not with wild-type p53; an alpha-specific Hsp90 antibody detected HSP90AA1 in the mutant-p53-containing ternary complex. The amount of Hsp90 bound to individual mutant p53 proteins correlated with their stability. Radicicol or geldanamycin disrupted the complex and promoted mutant-p53 polyubiquitination and degradation, while a p53/MDM2-double-null comparison showed that MDM2 was required for inhibitor-induced mutant-p53 turnover. This is strong mutant-specific HSP90AA1-tested client and stability evidence.

Hsp90 overexpression increased TTK protein, Hsp90 knockdown reduced it, and geldanamycin or 17-AAG depleted overexpressed TTK. MG132 rescued inhibitor-induced TTK loss, while anti-Hsp90 immunoprecipitation recovered TTK and Hsp90 inhibitors weakened that association. Hsp90 inhibition also reversed TTK-driven cell-cycle, survival, proliferation, and xenograft phenotypes. Together these data support TTK as a stability-dependent cytosolic HSP90 client in osteosarcoma, with broad-HSP90 rather than defensible alpha- or beta-specific scope.

Tandem affinity purification of tagged full-length USP50 from U2OS cells recovered HSP90-beta as a major band identified by ten peptides, and an independent USP50-bait yeast-two-hybrid screen recovered HSP90-alpha and HSP90-beta 25 and 32 times, respectively. USP50 depletion reduced Wee1 abundance, with partial MG132 rescue, and enhanced checkpoint bypass, leading the authors to propose that USP50 regulates assembly or function of an HSP90-Wee1 complex. The two orthogonal pair assays strongly support alpha- and beta-resolved USP50 association, while the complex-regulatory mechanism remains indirect.

In yeast expressing oncogenic v-Src, anti-v-Src immunoprecipitation recovered both Hsp90 and Cdc37. VCP co-occurred with Hsp90, CDC37, FKBP52, and p23 in native chaperone heterocomplexes; salt and inhibitor tests distinguished the VCP-containing complex from a canonical unstable client complex.

Broad HSP90 and vimentin co-localized and reciprocally co-immunoprecipitated. Geldanamycin caused caspase-dependent vimentin loss during apoptosis; broad HSP90 antisense enhanced cleavage, while an explicitly full-length human HSP90alpha construct reduced cleavage and cell death. This supports an alpha-resolved protective degradation/stability relationship in this stress context, not client status.

Additional experiments place Aha1 with selected Hsp90 cochaperones and show functional effects on Hsp90-dependent luciferase renaturation. The source strongly supports AHSA1 as a broad Hsp90 cochaperone but does not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1.

Amyloid-beta reduced Hsp90, TERT protein, and telomerase activity in murine cerebral endothelial cells. These current orthogonal perturbations support TERT as a broad cytosolic-Hsp90 client whose stability and enzymatic activity depend on the Hsp90 system in this stress model.
